clue.text: On reflection, gang needs to accept bereavement to flourish

indicators.note: the reversed gang word takes in, or accepts, the bereavement word
a reflection shows a thing back to front, so the word for gang is read backwards

parts.note: a mob is a gang
a bereavement is a loss

explanation.surface: A gang must come to terms with a death before it can thrive again.
explanation.definitionFit: To blossom is to bloom or thrive, a synonym for flourish as a verb.

clue.text: Cross bishop breathes irregularly etc

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
to be alive is to breathe, so breathes stands for is

indicators.note: irregularly says the three letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An irritated bishop is breathing unevenly, and so on.
explanation.walkthrough: Cross looks like 'angry', but it is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To bisect a line is to cut across it, dividing it in two.

clue.text: Painting has the power that a mechanic could make good use of

definitions.text: that a mechanic could make good use of

parts.note: an oil is an oil painting
can means is able, has the power to

explanation.surface: A painting that a mechanic could put to good use.
explanation.definitionFit: An oilcan is a container with a spout for lubricating machinery parts.

clue.text: Shock — southern ladies running riot round prison!

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go round the prison word
running riot means acting wildly, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: the can is slang for prison

explanation.surface: Southern women run wild around a jail, to everyone's horror.
explanation.walkthrough: The can is American slang for jail; it goes round-wise inside the southern-plus-scrambled-ladies string, straight after its opening letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To scandalise people is to outrage or appal them.

clue.text: Decoration somehow made large

indicators.note: somehow says the letters come together in some other order

parts.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A decoration made big in some way.
explanation.definitionFit: A medal is an honour pinned on a uniform, a military decoration.

clue.text: Island's problem with American transport: no terminus

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem

indicators.note: terminus means end, so the transport word loses its final letter

parts.note: a tram is a form of public transport

explanation.surface: An island's difficulties with its American-style trams, which never reach the end of the line.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after Island stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Sumatra is a large Indonesian island, so this is a definition by example.

clue.text: Vehicle's way over left side of carriageway, by a river

indicators.note: in a down entry the street comes above the next part

parts.note: a street is a way or road

indicators.note: the left side of a word is its first letter

parts.note: R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A vehicle's road crosses to the left side of the carriageway beside a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A streetcar is the American name for a tram, a passenger vehicle on rails.

clue.text: Classic story: Short Time from the pen of Francis?

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a short time
a book written by someone is from their pen
Dick Francis was a British jockey turned thriller writer

explanation.surface: A classic tale called Short Time by the novelist Francis.
explanation.walkthrough: Dick Francis was a jockey who wrote horse-racing thrillers, so 'from the pen of Francis' reads as BY DICK.
explanation.definitionFit: Moby-Dick is Herman Melville's classic novel about the white whale.

clue.text: Time's against Shakespeare's wife? Husband's off in the direction indicated

indicators.note: against means next to, so the time letter sits beside the wife's name
off says the husband letter departs from the name

parts.note: Anne Hathaway was Shakespeare's wife

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's wife turns against time, while her husband has gone off somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: The H that leaves is the second one in HATHAWAY. The answer is a Western phrase, 'they went thataway'.
explanation.definitionFit: Thataway is a jokey cowboy word meaning in that direction, said while pointing.

clue.text: Recklessness of car almost hitting a centre of population

indicators.note: almost drops the last letter

parts.note: an Audi is a make of car
a city is a large centre of population

explanation.surface: A reckless driver's car nearly crashes into a town centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Audacity is daring boldness, a willingness to take risks.

clue.text: A second city's somersaulting dance

indicators.note: a somersault turns head over heels, so the whole string is read backwards

parts.note: LA is the city Los Angeles, and with the 's it gives LAS

explanation.surface: A second city has a tumbling dance of its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Salsa is a lively Latin American dance, so this is an example of the category.

clue.text: Fly with management, a feature of which is doubles all round!

definitions.text: a feature of which is doubles all round!

parts.note: to dart is to fly or move swiftly
the board is a company's management

explanation.surface: A rushing executive with a board that orders double drinks for everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doubles all round' sounds like a round of drinks, but a darts board has a ring of double-score spaces around its edge.
explanation.definitionFit: The outer ring of a darts target is the doubles ring, which runs right round the circle.

clue.text: Light composition of Rice, incorporating classical composer

indicators.note: the rearranged letters take the composer inside them
a composition is a putting-together, so the letters of the name are rearranged

parts.note: Handel was a German-born Baroque composer

explanation.surface: Tim Rice writes a song that draws on a classical composer's work.
explanation.walkthrough: Rice is Tim Rice, the lyricist who worked with Andrew Lloyd Webber, so the surface reads as a musical in the making.
explanation.definitionFit: A chandelier is a hanging light fitting with several branches.

clue.text: Powder used by first alchemists

indicators.note: used by says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A powder that the earliest alchemists worked with.
explanation.definitionFit: Talc is a soft mineral ground into talcum powder for the skin.

clue.text: Marry Hitch? Perhaps, but it's not indicative of a steady heart

definitions.text: not indicative of a steady heart

indicators.note: perhaps says the letters might be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: Getting married might set the heart racing rather than keep it steady.
explanation.definitionFit: An arrhythmic heartbeat is irregular, lacking a steady rhythm.

clue.text: Raven, dog and rodent eating new fruit

parts.note: raven describes a glossy black colour
a cur is a mongrel dog

indicators.note: the rodent takes in, or eats, the letter for new

parts.note: a rat is a rodent

explanation.surface: A raven, a dog and a rat all tucking into some fresh fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: Raven looks like the bird but stands for the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A blackcurrant is a small dark berry grown on a garden bush.

clue.text: Old playwright having no bottle has eg a whisky accompaniment

parts.note: Noël Coward was an English playwright of the last century
ice is often added to whisky

explanation.surface: A dead playwright without the nerve takes his whisky with something on the side.
explanation.walkthrough: Bottle is British slang for courage, so no bottle is a lack of nerve.
explanation.definitionFit: Cowardice is a lack of courage, which British slang calls having no bottle.

clue.text: Work period top protection wear for the Met?

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
an era is a period of time
a hat protects the top of the head

explanation.surface: A spell of work guarding the top, kit worn at the Met.
explanation.walkthrough: The Met is New York's Metropolitan Opera, not the London police.
explanation.definitionFit: An opera hat is a collapsible top hat once worn to evening performances at the opera.

clue.text: Has life in Cairns destroyed flowers?

indicators.note: the life word goes inside the scrambled letters
destroyed says the town's letters are broken up and reassembled

parts.note: to be is to exist, to have life

explanation.surface: Has something living in the Queensland city of Cairns wrecked the flowers?
explanation.walkthrough: Cairns is a city in Queensland, Australia; the question mark fits the surface's puzzled gardener, not the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Narcissi are spring flowers such as daffodils and jonquils.

clue.text: Honourable dignitary's after power lift

indicators.note: the dignitary is placed after the power and lift pieces

parts.note: to raise is to lift
a worthy is a dignitary or notable person

explanation.surface: An honourable official wants a boost to the electricity supply.
explanation.definitionFit: Praiseworthy means deserving praise, close in sense to honourable or creditable.

clue.text: Take criminally bad union leader before court

indicators.note: acting criminally is going wrong, so the letters are rearranged
the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Kidnapping a crooked trade-union boss before he can appear in court.
explanation.definitionFit: To abduct someone is to carry them off by force, a narrow sense of take.

clue.text: Strong Brussels youth raised in a medieval way

parts.note: F is forte, the musical term for loud or strong
Brussels is the seat of the European Union, EU

indicators.note: in a down entry raised means read upwards, so the letters go backwards

parts.note: a lad is a youth

explanation.surface: A sturdy Belgian lad brought up the old-fashioned way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a ... way' only links the parts.
explanation.definitionFit: The feudal system of lords and vassals belongs to the Middle Ages.

clue.text: Off-colour and about to enter shaft

indicators.note: the short word for about goes inside the shaft word

parts.note: a ray is a shaft of light
C is short for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: Feeling unwell and about to go down a mine shaft.
explanation.walkthrough: Off-colour looks like feeling unwell, but it means risqué here.
explanation.definitionFit: An off-colour joke is a racy, slightly indecent one.

clue.text: Paying for fine inlaid top furniture item

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a table is an item of furniture

explanation.surface: Handing over money for a fine inlaid tabletop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inlaid top' looks like a description of the furniture; it is the first letter of inlaid.
explanation.definitionFit: A profitable business is one that pays, making money for its owners.

clue.text: Bill's comparatively astute

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a printed handbill or leaflet
second meaning: more fly, fly being slang for sharp

explanation.walkthrough: Fly is British slang for knowing or shrewd, so its comparative is more astute.
explanation.definitionFit: A flyer is a handbill, and as an adjective's comparative it means sharper or shrewder.

clue.text: See 6
Bad feeling of many against independence leader — one from Italy, maybe

parts.note: a host is a large number, a multitude

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter
maybe says the remaining letters could be arranged another way
one is taken out of the country's name

parts.note: A means one, as in a single thing

explanation.surface: Resentment among many people towards an independence leader, perhaps an Italian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From' removes A (one) from ITALY to leave ITLY, and 'maybe' rearranges that to LITY.
explanation.definitionFit: Hostility is enmity or antagonism, ill will between people.

clue.text: Fungus shape

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a furry fungal growth
second meaning: to form or model

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a noun for a fungal growth on food and a verb meaning to form something.

clue.text: Drop gets player finally into touch

indicators.note: the letter goes inside the touch word

parts.note: to tickle is to touch lightly

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of player

explanation.surface: A footballer scores by getting the ball into touch.
explanation.definitionFit: A trickle is a thin flow, a drop or small amount of liquid.

clue.text: Playing clarinet and briefly leaving performance

indicators.note: playing says the instrument's letters are worked into a new arrangement
the short form of and departs from the instrument's letters

parts.note: N is the shortened and, as in rock 'n' roll

explanation.surface: A clarinettist plays and then quickly leaves the concert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'And briefly' is N, as in rock 'n' roll; 'leaving' takes it out of CLARINET, and 'Playing' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A recital is a musical performance, often by a single soloist.
